entities.name: Mycetoma
entities.description: A chronic, progressively destructive, indolent granulomatous inflammatory disease of subcutaneous tissues, skin, and underlying bone, endemic within the tropical and subtropical Mycetoma Belt, caused by true filamentous fungi (eumycetoma) or aerobic actinomycete bacteria (actinomycetoma).

entities.name: Madura foot
entities.description: Progressive chronic swelling, deformity, and fistulizing involvement of the foot, representing the most common anatomical site of mycetoma infection.

entities.name: Pedal tumefaction
entities.description: Subcutaneous, slowly enlarging mass or localized tumefactive enlargement localized to the foot.

entities.name: Plantar subcutaneous nodules
entities.description: Firm, non-tender subcutaneous nodular aggregates situated along the plantar aspect of the foot.

entities.name: Dorsal foot fistulae
entities.description: Cutaneous draining fistulous orifices situated along the dorsal aspect of the foot.

entities.name: Eumycetoma
entities.description: Chronic subcutaneous granulomatous mycetoma caused by true filamentous fungi such as Madurella species.

entities.name: Actinomycetoma
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous infection caused by aerobic branching actinomycete bacteria such as Actinomadura, Nocardia, or Streptomyces.

entities.name: Black grain eumycetoma
entities.description: Fungal mycetoma sub-entity characterized by macroscopic black granules composed of dark pigmented fungal hyphae.

entities.name: White grain eumycetoma
entities.description: Fungal mycetoma sub-entity producing non-pigmented white to yellowish granules consisting of hyaline fungal hyphae.

entities.name: Red grain actinomycetoma
entities.description: Aggressive bacterial mycetoma variant characterized by bright red to crimson grains and extensive osteolysis.

entities.name: Yellow grain actinomycetoma
entities.description: Bacterial mycetoma variant discharging pale, yellow, or light brownish microcolonies.

entities.name: Tarsal bone osteolysis
entities.description: Destructive osteolytic resorption and cavitary remodeling affecting the tarsal bones of the foot.

entities.name: Metatarsal bone cavitation
entities.description: Formation of rounded punched-out cystic cavities within the metatarsal bones.

entities.name: Cortical bone destruction
entities.description: Erosive dissolution of the outer bony cortex mediated by chronic granulomatous infiltration.

entities.name: Periosteal new bone
entities.description: Reactive osteoblastic new bone deposition along cortical surfaces adjacent to chronic infection.

entities.name: Fascial plane invasion
entities.description: Infiltration and longitudinal tracking of granulomatous infection along deep connective tissue fascial planes.

entities.name: Intermuscular septum extension
entities.description: Pathological tracking of mycetoma granulomas across intermuscular fascial septa.

entities.name: Hand mycetoma
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous tumefaction, sinus formation, and grain discharge localized to the hand.

entities.name: Palmar subcutaneous nodules
entities.description: Subcutaneous nodular lesions situated within the palmar and thenar compartments of the hand.

entities.name: Wrist joint stiffness
entities.description: Progressive restriction of wrist joint mobility secondary to periarticular fibrosis and carpal invasion.

entities.name: Tibial cortical invasion
entities.description: Direct invasion and osteolytic erosion of the tibial shaft and pretibial periosteum.

entities.name: Knee joint deformity
entities.description: Structural distortion and flexural contracture of the knee joint caused by adjacent granulomatous disease.

entities.name: Gluteal subcutaneous mass
entities.description: Large, indurated subcutaneous tumefactive mass situated within the gluteal and buttock musculature.

entities.name: Dorsal trunk tumefaction
entities.description: Indurated nodular tumefactive lesions distributed across the posterior thoracic and lumbar trunk.

entities.name: Shoulder soft-tissue mass
entities.description: Granulomatous subcutaneous tumefaction overlying the shoulder girdle and scapular region.

entities.name: Abdominal wall induration
entities.description: Dense subcutaneous woody induration and fistulizing disease involving the anterior abdominal wall.

entities.name: Lumbar spine invasion
entities.description: Contiguous infiltration and osteolytic destruction of the lumbar vertebrae and paraspinal soft tissues.

entities.name: Cranial bone involvement
entities.description: Osteolytic invasion and cavitary erosion of the skull bones secondary to contiguous scalp infection.

entities.name: Regional lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlargement of regional draining lymph nodes adjacent to active mycetoma lesions.

entities.name: Inguinal lymph node enlargement
entities.description: Painless or tender reactive enlargement of inguinal lymph nodes draining lower extremity mycetoma.

entities.name: Epitrochlear lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlargement of the epitrochlear lymph node draining mycetoma lesions of the hand and forearm.

entities.name: Secondary bacterial infection
entities.description: Superimposed pyogenic bacterial infection complicating chronic open cutaneous sinus tracts.

entities.name: Staphylococcal superinfection
entities.description: Superimposed Staphylococcus aureus infection of sinuses predisposing to systemic bacteremia and abscesses.

entities.name: Purulent exudate discharge
entities.description: Thick purulent or serosanguinous fluid drained through open cutaneous fistulae carrying organism grains.

entities.name: Tendon sheath infiltration
entities.description: Contiguous granulomatous spread along and within tenosynovial sheaths.

entities.name: Soft tissue fibrosis
entities.description: Extensive fibroblastic collagen deposition and cicatricial remodeling of infected subcutaneous tissues.

entities.name: Limb motor disability
entities.description: Functional impairment and loss of motor capability in the affected anatomical extremity.

entities.name: Grotesque limb deformity
entities.description: Severe architectural distortion and massive disfiguring enlargement of the infected limb.

entities.name: Late periosteal pain
entities.description: Deep aching somatic pain developing in late-stage disease due to cortical bone expansion and periosteal tension.

entities.name: Chronic muscle wasting
entities.description: Progressive muscular atrophy of the affected limb resulting from prolonged immobility and chronic granulomatous disuse.

entities.name: Severe localized immobility
entities.description: Complete loss of functional ambulation or joint movement localized to the affected extremity.

entities.name: Cardinal diagnostic triad
entities.description: The pathognomonic physical triad of mycetoma: painless subcutaneous mass, multiple sinus tracts, and grain discharge.

entities.name: Painless subcutaneous tumefaction
entities.description: Indolent, non-tender, slow-growing subcutaneous swelling characteristic of early-to-mid stage mycetoma.

entities.name: Multiple draining sinuses
entities.description: Plurality of cutaneous fistulous tracts that discharge exudate containing organisms.

entities.name: Macroscopic grain discharge
entities.description: Extrusion of macroscopic visible grains or microcolonies from active sinus tracts.

entities.name: Discharging black grains
entities.description: Exuded dark brown to coal-black visible grains pathognomonic of dematiaceous fungal eumycetoma.

entities.name: Discharging bright red grains
entities.description: Exuded brilliant crimson-red macroscopic grains diagnostic of Actinomadura pelletieri actinomycetoma.

entities.name: Discharging pale yellow grains
entities.description: Macroscopic pale yellow or ochre-colored granules discharged from active sinus tracts.

entities.name: Discharging chalky white grains
entities.description: Macroscopic chalky white or cream-colored grains extruded from sinus tracts.

entities.name: Hard cement-bound grains
entities.description: Rigid, brittle granules bound by an internal interstitial melanized cement matrix.

entities.name: Woody subcutaneous induration
entities.description: Firm, non-yielding, woody induration of the subcutaneous tissue upon physical palpation.

entities.name: Crateriform sinus openings
entities.description: Elevated, crater-like papular cutaneous orifices with central discharging pore.

entities.name: Interconnected fistulous tracts
entities.description: Subcutaneous branching network of interconnected sinus tracts communicating across tissue planes.

entities.name: Serosanguinous sinus drainage
entities.description: Thin, blood-tinged serous discharge flowing from active cutaneous sinus tracts.

entities.name: Oily purulent discharge
entities.description: Viscous, oily, purulent exudate extruded from chronic mycetoma sinus tracts.

entities.name: Striking absence of pain
entities.description: Marked lack of physical tenderness or spontaneous pain despite massive tissue tumefaction and bone destruction.

entities.name: Afebrile clinical presentation
entities.description: Complete absence of systemic pyrexia or constitutional febrile signs in uncomplicated mycetoma.

entities.name: Absence of erythema
entities.description: Lack of intense cutaneous redness or acute erythematous flare surrounding the subcutaneous mass.

entities.name: Local skin hyperpigmentation
entities.description: Localized darkening and hypermelanosis of the cutaneous surface overlying chronic mycetoma lesions.

entities.name: Cutaneous tethering to mass
entities.description: Pathological adherence and tethering of the epidermis and dermis to underlying fibrous tumefaction.

entities.name: Deep fascial fixation
entities.description: Rigid fixation of the subcutaneous mass to deep muscular aponeuroses and periosteal layers.

entities.name: Puckered scar orifices
entities.description: Retracted, pitted, puckered cutaneous scars marking sites of previously closed sinus tracts.

entities.name: Lobulated subcutaneous contours
entities.description: Irregular, lobular, multinodular surface texture palpable across the tumefactive swelling.

entities.name: Preserved distal peripheral sensation
entities.description: Preservation of distal touch, pinprick, and temperature sensation despite massive localized pedal deformity.

entities.name: Preserved peripheral arterial pulses
entities.description: Intact palpable arterial pulsations in the distal extremity, confirming patent main arterial vasculature.

entities.name: Painless regional lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Non-tender, indolent enlargement of regional lymph nodes draining chronic mycetoma lesions.

entities.name: Firm mobile sentinel nodules
entities.description: Discrete, firm, bead-like satellite nodules palpable along proximal lymphatic drainage pathways.

entities.name: Normal local skin temperature
entities.description: Normal cutaneous thermal examination over the tumefaction without localized inflammatory hyperthermia.

entities.name: False healing with scarring
entities.description: Cyclical phenomenon of transient sinus closure followed by recurrent rupture and active discharge.

entities.name: MRI dot-in-circle sign
entities.description: Pathognomonic MRI sign consisting of high-intensity round spheres containing central punctate low-signal dots representing grains.

entities.name: T2-weighted hyperintense round granulomas
entities.description: High signal intensity rounded spherical lesions visualized on T2-weighted magnetic resonance images.

entities.name: Central hypointense grain dot
entities.description: Punctate, low-signal center within high-signal granulomatous cavities corresponding to the causative grain.

entities.name: Peripheral gadolinium rim enhancement
entities.description: Ring-like enhancement pattern observed along the margins of mycetoma granulomas following gadolinium administration.

entities.name: Ultrasound dot-in-circle sign
entities.description: High-resolution ultrasound feature showing round hypoechoic granulomas with central hyper-reflective echoes representing grains.

entities.name: Central hyper-reflective echoes
entities.description: Bright, echogenic foci within hypoechoic cystic cavities corresponding to mycetoma grains on ultrasonography.

entities.name: Posterior acoustic shadowing
entities.description: Sonographic acoustic attenuation and shadowing cast deep to dense, cement-rich mycetoma grains.

entities.name: Thick-walled hypoechoic granulomas
entities.description: Well-circumscribed hypoechoic fluid cavities bounded by prominent echogenic fibrous capsules.

entities.name: Ill-defined hypoechoic infiltrates
entities.description: Poorly demarcated, non-encapsulated hypoechoic infiltrates characteristic of bacterial actinomycetoma on ultrasound.

entities.name: Moth-eaten bone appearance
entities.description: Radiographic pattern of diffuse, irregular osteolytic osseous destruction resembling moth-eaten cloth.

entities.name: Punched-out osteolytic geodes
entities.description: Round, sharply defined osteolytic cavities ('geodes') within trabecular bone surrounded by reactive sclerosis.

entities.name: Periosteal cortical bone reaction
entities.description: Reactive periosteal bone thickening and spiculation visible on plain radiographs and CT.

entities.name: Preserved articular joint spaces
entities.description: Remarkable sparing and preservation of articular cartilage and joint spaces until advanced end-stage disease.

entities.name: Soft tissue plane obliteration
entities.description: Loss of normal radiolucent fat planes and fascial margins on plain radiography of the extremity.

entities.name: Cortical bone remodeling
entities.description: Structural distortion, expansion, and remodeled architecture of cortical bones seen on radiography.

entities.name: CT cortical bone erosion
entities.description: High-resolution computed tomography demonstration of cortical osteolytic defects and bony discontinuities.

entities.name: CT soft-tissue infiltration
entities.description: Computed tomographic cross-sectional depiction of granulomatous soft-tissue masses and tracking sinuses.

entities.name: Direct grain wet mount
entities.description: Bedside microscopic examination of freshly collected grains suspended in saline or water.

entities.name: Potassium hydroxide grain mount
entities.description: Microscopic preparation utilizing potassium hydroxide to dissolve host keratin and reveal fungal morphology.

entities.name: Broad septate fungal hyphae
entities.description: Thick, branched, septate fungal filaments measuring 2 to 6 microns in width observed within grains.

entities.name: Vesicular swollen chlamydoconidia
entities.description: Globular, vesicular, thick-walled swollen fungal cells found within eumycetoma grains.

entities.name: Brown-black cement matrix
entities.description: Dense, dark, melanized amorphous cement material holding fungal hyphae together within black grains.

entities.name: Delicate Gram-positive filaments
entities.description: Slender, branching bacterial filaments measuring less than 1 micrometer in diameter stained Gram-positive.

entities.name: Branching bacterial microcolonies
entities.description: Densely packed aggregates of filamentous bacteria displaying radial branching.

entities.name: Modified Kinyoun stain positivity
entities.description: Positive acid-fast staining using modified Kinyoun protocol with weak acid decolorization.

entities.name: Partially acid-fast filaments
entities.description: Delicate, beaded, branching bacterial filaments retaining carbolfuchsin under weak acid decolorization.

entities.name: Suppurative granulomatous reaction
entities.description: Histopathological pattern composed of central neutrophilic abscesses surrounded by epithelioid granulomas.

entities.name: Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon
entities.description: Radiating intensely eosinophilic antibody-antigen precipitate surrounding microbial grains in tissue sections.

entities.name: PAS-positive fungal elements
entities.description: Vivid magenta staining of fungal cell walls in tissue sections using Periodic Acid-Schiff stain.

entities.name: Grocott methenamine silver positivity
entities.description: Black silver impregnation of fungal cell walls using Grocott's methenamine silver histochemical stain.

entities.name: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate elevation
entities.description: Elevation of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (typically 40 to 80 mm/h) as a marker of chronic inflammation.

entities.name: Normal peripheral leukocyte count
entities.description: Total white blood cell count remaining within standard reference ranges despite extensive local infection.

entities.name: Absence of peripheral eosinophilia
entities.description: Normal peripheral absolute eosinophil count without systemic eosinophilic leukocytosis.

entities.name: Absence of neutrophilia
entities.description: Normal absolute neutrophil counts without bandemia or toxic granulations.

entities.name: Normocytic normochromic anemia
entities.description: Mild normocytic anemia occurring secondary to chronic localized inflammatory cytokine release.

entities.name: Fine-needle aspiration grain cytology
entities.description: Cytological aspiration of intact subcutaneous nodules to retrieve diagnostic grains for direct microscopy.

entities.name: Deep surgical biopsy histopathology
entities.description: Formal surgical wedge biopsy of deep subcutaneous and osseous tissue for definitive histopathological diagnosis.

entities.name: Fungal culture on Sabouraud
entities.description: Microbiological fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar yielding characteristic slow-growing colonies.

entities.name: The Mycetoma Belt
entities.description: Geographic hyperendemic zone between latitudes 15°S and 30°N with arid climate and high mycetoma incidence.

entities.name: Arid and semi-arid climates
entities.description: Climatic environments with low annual rainfall (50-500 mm) and prolonged hot dry seasons.

entities.name: Acacia nilotica thorns
entities.description: Sharp, rigid thorns of Acacia nilotica trees acting as mechanical vectors for fungal and bacterial inoculation.

entities.name: Minor penetrating skin trauma
entities.description: Mechanical percutaneous puncture wounds or abrasions allowing subcutaneous entry of environmental pathogens.

entities.name: Barefoot walking
entities.description: Habitual ambulation without protective footwear, predisposing the feet to thorn and wood splinter punctures.

entities.name: Soil-dwelling microorganisms
entities.description: Saprophytic geophilic bacteria and fungi inhabiting dry tropical soils and thorny plant debris.

entities.name: Dry plant splinters
entities.description: Vegetable splinters and sharp dried botanical fragments capable of inoculating pathogens into skin.

entities.name: Wood chips
entities.description: Sharp wood fragments and timber chips carrying environmental saprophytes into broken skin.

entities.name: Carrying thorny firewood
entities.description: Manual transport of thorny branches and wood bundles on the bare shoulders and back.

entities.name: Carrying soil-laden crop sacks
entities.description: Occupational carrying of heavy, soil-contaminated grain or produce sacks across the trunk.

entities.name: Sudan Gezira state
entities.description: The central agricultural state of Sudan, representing the single largest global epicenter of eumycetoma.

entities.name: Central and northern Mexico
entities.description: Arid agricultural zones of Mexico representing the leading global endemic region for bacterial actinomycetoma.

entities.name: Arid northwest India
entities.description: Arid desert and semi-arid scrub regions of northwestern India with high endemic mycetoma rates.

entities.name: Rural subsistence farmers
entities.description: Subsistence agricultural workers working barefoot in endemic soil and thorny fields.

entities.name: Field agricultural laborers
entities.description: Manual farm workers engaged in heavy land clearing, planting, and harvesting in endemic areas.

entities.name: Nomadic livestock pastoralists
entities.description: Nomadic and semi-nomadic herdsmen herding animals across dry acacia scrub.

entities.name: Young adult males
entities.description: Young male demographic group aged 15-40 years with highest occupational outdoor exposure.

entities.name: Impoverished rural communities
entities.description: Socioeconomically disadvantaged rural populations with limited access to footwear and health infrastructure.

entities.name: Indolent multi-year incubation
entities.description: Protracted, insidious incubation period lasting from many months to multiple years before clinical presentation.

entities.name: Average two-to-five-year onset
entities.description: Typical clinical time window (mean 2 to 5 years) elapsing between inoculating trauma and definitive hospital diagnosis.

entities.name: Subcutaneous fungal dormancy
entities.description: Extended period of slow microbial growth and cement deposition within subcutaneous tissues prior to sinus rupture.

entities.name: Non-contagious transmission
entities.description: Absence of direct human-to-human communicability; infection occurs exclusively via environmental inoculation.

entities.name: Acute rapid progression
entities.description: Sudden or rapid clinical evolution over days to weeks, inconsistent with indolent mycetoma.

entities.name: Acute severe localized pain
entities.description: Early, excruciating, or throbbing localized physical pain at initial clinical presentation.

entities.name: High spiking fevers
entities.description: Marked systemic fevers, chills, and rigors, indicating acute pyogenic sepsis rather than mycetoma.

entities.name: Marked neutrophilic leukocytosis
entities.description: Prominent systemic elevation of neutrophil counts with toxic left shift and bandemia.

entities.name: Complete absence of grains
entities.description: Persistent absence of visible or microscopic bacterial or fungal granules in sinus exudate.

entities.name: Rapid hematogenous dissemination
entities.description: Early widespread vascular or hematogenous dissemination to internal solid organs.

entities.name: Medlar bodies copper pennies
entities.description: Diagnostic golden-brown thick-walled muriform cells ('copper pennies') pathognomonic of chromoblastomycosis.

entities.name: Acute fluctuant pyogenic abscess
entities.description: Rapidly developing, warm, fluctuant, painful purulent collection characteristic of acute pyogenic infection.

entities.name: Rapid necrotizing ulceration
entities.description: Rapid, destructive, full-thickness cutaneous ulceration and gangrenous necrosis.

entities.name: Human-to-human transmission
entities.description: Direct communicability or secondary transmission between human contacts.

entities.name: Bilateral ascending lymphedema
entities.description: Symmetrical, diffuse, bilateral ascending lymphedematous swelling lacking localized sinuses or grains.

entities.name: Caseating granulomas with AFB
entities.description: Caseous necrotic granulomas demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on standard Ziehl-Neelsen stain.

entities.name: Malignant anaplastic spindle cells
entities.description: Histopathological demonstration of neoplastic, pleomorphic anaplastic cells and osteoid production.

entities.name: Spontaneous clinical resolution
entities.description: Spontaneous, complete involution of lesions without specific medical or surgical therapy.

entities.name: Mucocutaneous midface destruction
entities.description: Destructive ulcerating lesions of the nasal septum, palate, and midface mucosa ('espundia').

entities.name: Purely superficial verrucous plaques
entities.description: Warty, hyperkeratotic plaques strictly limited to the epidermis lacking deep fascial involvement.

entities.name: Painful regional lymphadenitis
entities.description: Acute, tender, fluctuant inflammatory lymphadenitis characteristic of pyogenic or venereal infections.

entities.name: Diffuse systemic toxic shock
entities.description: Hemodynamic collapse, refractory hypotension, and multiorgan failure of acute septic etiology.

entities.name: Rapid response to penicillin
entities.description: Prompt, complete disease resolution following short-course standard penicillin treatment.

entities.name: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilaremia
entities.description: Circulating sheathed microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti in peripheral blood smears.

entities.name: Intraosseous sequestration without sinuses
entities.description: Isolated necrotic intraosseous bone sequestrum lacking cutaneous fistulization or grains.

entities.name: Spontaneous pulmonary metastatic nodules
entities.description: Disseminated spherical 'cannonball' parenchymal lung nodules of malignant metastatic origin.

entities.name: Chronic pyogenic osteomyelitis
entities.description: Chronic bacterial infection of bone characterized by severe pain, sequestra, involucra, and purulent discharge without grains.

entities.name: Chromoblastomycosis
entities.description: Subcutaneous dematiaceous fungal infection producing superficial hyperkeratotic verrucous plaques and diagnostic medlar bodies.

entities.name: Osteosarcoma
entities.description: Primary malignant bone neoplasm producing osteoid matrix and aggressive periosteal reactions without draining sinuses.

entities.name: Kaposi Sarcoma
entities.description: Vascular neoplasm linked to human herpesvirus 8 producing multiple violaceous plaques and nodular lesions.

entities.name: Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic mycobacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis producing caseating granulomas and cold abscesses.

entities.name: Podoconiosis
entities.description: Non-infectious geochemically induced geochemical geochemical lymphedema affecting barefoot individuals on volcanic soils.

entities.name: Lymphatic Filariasis
entities.description: Mosquito-borne nematode infection causing lymphatic obstruction, massive elephantiasis, and hydrocele.

entities.name: Cutaneous leishmaniasis
entities.description: Protozoal skin infection transmitted by phlebotomine sandflies resulting in crusted, self-limiting or chronic cutaneous ulcers.

entities.name: Leprosy
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae primarily affecting peripheral nerves and skin.

entities.name: Soft tissue sarcoma
entities.description: Malignant mesenchymal neoplasm of connective tissues presenting as an expanding deep soft-tissue mass.

entities.name: Actinomycosis
entities.description: Chronic suppurative infection caused by endogenous anaerobic/microaerophilic Actinomyces species producing yellow sulfur granules.

entities.name: Sporotrichosis
entities.description: Subcutaneous mycosis caused by Sporothrix species characterized by ascending nodular lymphangitis.

entities.name: Bacterial cellulitis
entities.description: Acute spreading pyogenic bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous fat characterized by rubor, calor, and dolor.

entities.name: Buruli ulcer
entities.description: Destructive cutaneous mycobacterial disease caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans producing extensive undermined skin ulcers.

entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei in tropical soils presenting with pneumonia, septicemia, and multiple abscesses.

entities.name: Chondrosarcoma
entities.description: Malignant cartilaginous bone neoplasm characterized by lobular chondroid matrix mineralization without draining sinuses.

entities.name: Foreign body granuloma
entities.description: Localized non-infectious inflammatory reaction mounted against retained exogenous foreign material.

entities.name: Eumycetoma vs Actinomycetoma
entities.description: Critical clinical and microbiological distinction between fungal eumycetoma and bacterial actinomycetoma governing therapy.

relationships.keywords: madura foot, pedal tumefaction, chronic foot swelling
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma predominantly manifests as Madura foot, involving progressive swelling, deformity, and multiple draining sinus tracts of the foot and lower ankle in over 70% of cases.

relationships.keywords: tumefaction, foot swelling, painless nodule
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as gradual pedal tumefaction characterized by an indolent subcutaneous mass on the plantar or dorsal surface of the foot.

relationships.keywords: plantar nodules, deep subcutaneous mass, sol of foot
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma frequently manifests as firm plantar subcutaneous nodules that gradually coalesce to invade deep pedal fascial compartments.

relationships.keywords: dorsal foot, sinus tracts, cutaneous fistulae
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as multiple dorsal foot fistulae discharging purulent exudate and fungal or bacterial grains onto the skin surface.

relationships.keywords: eumycetoma, fungal mycetoma, fungal grain infection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as eumycetoma, a fungal etiology accounting for 40% of cases globally, characterized by encapsulated granulomas and melanized fungal grains.

relationships.keywords: actinomycetoma, bacterial mycetoma, actinomycete infection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as actinomycetoma, a bacterial etiology accounting for 60% of cases globally, characterized by aggressive osteolytic destruction and bacterial grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: black grains, Madurella mycetomatis, melanized fungi
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as black grain eumycetoma, predominantly caused by Madurella mycetomatis with dark melanized grains embedded in cemented matrix.

relationships.keywords: white grains, pale grains, Scedosporium, Acremonium
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as white grain eumycetoma, caused by hyaline fungi such as Scedosporium boydii and Acremonium falciforme forming pale granules.

relationships.keywords: red grains, Actinomadura pelletieri, crimson granules
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as red grain actinomycetoma, an aggressive form caused by Actinomadura pelletieri yielding brilliant crimson microcolonies.

relationships.keywords: yellow grains, Streptomyces, Actinomadura madurae
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as yellow grain actinomycetoma, caused by Streptomyces somaliensis, Nocardia brasiliensis, or Actinomadura madurae producing yellow-to-brown grains.

relationships.keywords: tarsal osteolysis, bone erosion, calcaneus destruction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as severe tarsal bone osteolysis as granulomatous inflammation erodes the calcaneus, talus, and cuboid bones.

relationships.keywords: metatarsal cavitation, geodes, punched-out bone
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as metatarsal bone cavitation with rounded osteolytic geodes and extensive cortical destruction of the forefoot bones.

relationships.keywords: cortical destruction, bone resorption, periosteal breach
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as cortical bone destruction as fungal hyphae and actinomycete filaments breach the periosteal sheath and invade medullary spaces.

relationships.keywords: periosteal reaction, new bone formation, hyperostosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as exuberant periosteal new bone formation surrounding areas of chronic cortical necrosis, producing bony expansion and sclerosis.

relationships.keywords: fascial invasion, deep tissue spread, interfascial tracking
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as extensive fascial plane invasion, spreading along deep plantar and crural aponeuroses without respecting anatomical boundaries.

relationships.keywords: intermuscular extension, muscular dissection, deep spread
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as intermuscular septum extension, dissecting between tendon sheaths and muscular compartments of the extremity.

relationships.keywords: hand mycetoma, upper extremity, palmar tumefaction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as hand mycetoma in 5-10% of cases, commonly following traumatic occupational hand inoculation in agricultural workers.

relationships.keywords: palmar nodules, thenar swelling, hand lesions
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as palmar subcutaneous nodules that produce contractures and progressive destruction of palmar aponeuroses.

relationships.keywords: wrist ankylosis, joint limitation, carpal involvement
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as wrist joint stiffness and functional ankylosis resulting from adjacent carpal bone osteolysis and soft tissue fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: tibial invasion, shin osteitis, lower leg osteolysis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as tibial cortical invasion, eroding the anterior tibial cortex with chronic discharging fistulae over the shin.

relationships.keywords: knee deformity, fixed flexion, joint contracture
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as knee joint deformity and fixed flexion contractures when infection ascends to the popliteal fossa and patellar tissues.

relationships.keywords: gluteal mass, buttock mycetoma, pelvic tumefaction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as a gluteal subcutaneous mass following percutaneous thorn trauma from sitting on contaminated vegetation or thorny scrub.

relationships.keywords: trunk tumefaction, back mycetoma, paraspinal mass
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as dorsal trunk tumefaction in rural laborers carrying thorny acacia branches and firewood sacks across their shoulders.

relationships.keywords: shoulder mass, deltoid swelling, scapular mycetoma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as an indolent shoulder soft-tissue mass with sinus tracts tracking into deltoid and scapular musculature.

relationships.keywords: abdominal wall, anterior trunk, subcutaneous plaque
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as abdominal wall induration and woody nodular infiltration tracking along the rectus sheath.

relationships.keywords: spine invasion, vertebral osteolysis, paraspinal sinus
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as direct lumbar spine invasion, eroding vertebral bodies and causing paraspinal sinus formation with neurological risk.

relationships.keywords: cranial mycetoma, skull invasion, scalp tumefaction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as cranial bone involvement in rare head presentations, causing calvarial osteolysis and discharging scalp fistulae.

relationships.keywords: lymphadenopathy, regional nodes, lymphatic spread
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as regional lymphadenopathy due to secondary bacterial superinfection or direct lymphatic grain transport, more common in actinomycetoma.

relationships.keywords: inguinal nodes, groin swelling, lower limb drainage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as inguinal lymph node enlargement draining longstanding lower limb and foot disease.

relationships.keywords: epitrochlear node, elbow node, upper extremity drainage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as epitrochlear lymphadenopathy in upper extremity and hand infections due to proximal lymphatic drainage.

relationships.keywords: secondary infection, staphylococcus, cellulitis, pus
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as secondary bacterial infection, leading to acute purulent drainage, inflammatory pain, and potential septic complications.

relationships.keywords: staph aureus, superinfection, bacteremia risk
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as staphylococcal superinfection introduced through chronic open draining sinuses, converting painless disease to acute painful cellulitis.

relationships.keywords: purulent exudate, sinus pus, grain suspension
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as purulent exudate discharge that suspends infectious grains and continually oozes from active sinus orifices.

relationships.keywords: tendon sheath, tenosynovial spread, tendon destruction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as tendon sheath infiltration, tracking along flexor and extensor retinacula to compromise fine motor mobility.

relationships.keywords: tissue fibrosis, woody scarring, cicatrization
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as dense soft tissue fibrosis and cicatrization, encasing vascular bundles and freezing adjacent tendons.

relationships.keywords: motor disability, functional loss, foot drop
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as progressive limb motor disability resulting from muscle atrophy, tendon tethering, and skeletal distortion.

relationships.keywords: grotesque deformity, massive swelling, limb enlargement
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as grotesque limb deformity with bulbous enlargement, loss of normal anatomical contours, and woody pedal expansion.

relationships.keywords: late pain, periosteal stretch, deep bone ache
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as late periosteal pain arising after years of painless indolence due to extensive cortical stretch and secondary pyogenic osteitis.

relationships.keywords: muscle wasting, disuse atrophy, calf atrophy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as chronic muscle wasting and calf disuse atrophy proximal to the fixed, immobilized, and deformed foot.

relationships.keywords: localized immobility, joint fixation, walking inability
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycetoma manifests as severe localized immobility, rendering patients unable to bear weight or walk without crutches in advanced presentations.

relationships.keywords: cardinal triad, diagnostic triad, pathognomonic triad
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma possesses the cardinal diagnostic triad of a painless subcutaneous tumefaction, multiple discharging cutaneous sinuses, and macroscopic pigmented grains.

relationships.keywords: painless mass, tumefaction, cold nodule
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma features a painless subcutaneous tumefaction that grows insidiously over months or years without provoking acute inflammatory tenderness.

relationships.keywords: multiple sinuses, sinus tracts, discharging fistulae
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma exhibits multiple draining sinuses distributed across the tumefactive surface, cyclically discharging and healing with characteristic puckered scars.

relationships.keywords: grain discharge, macroscopic granules, fungal grains
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma features macroscopic grain discharge from cutaneous sinuses, yielding visible bacterial or fungal microcolonies 0.5 to 2 mm in diameter.

relationships.keywords: black grains, Madurella grains, melanized grains
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma exhibits discharging black grains pathognomonic of eumycetoma caused by Madurella mycetomatis or Trematosphaeria grisea.

relationships.keywords: red grains, Actinomadura pelletieri, crimson granules
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma exhibits discharging bright red grains pathognomonic of aggressive actinomycetoma caused by Actinomadura pelletieri.

relationships.keywords: yellow grains, Streptomyces grains, pale granules
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma exhibits discharging pale yellow grains indicating actinomycetoma (Streptomyces somaliensis, Nocardia) or occasionally white-grain eumycetoma.

relationships.keywords: white grains, Scedosporium, Actinomadura madurae
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma exhibits discharging chalky white grains produced by Actinomadura madurae, Nocardia brasiliensis, or fungal Scedosporium boydii.

relationships.keywords: cement matrix, hard grains, melanized cement
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma yields hard cement-bound grains that resist mechanical crushing on a glass slide, characteristic of Madurella mycetomatis.

relationships.keywords: woody induration, brawny induration, firm mass
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma manifests woody subcutaneous induration on palpation, feeling firm, leathery, and anchored to underlying osteofascial structures.

relationships.keywords: crateriform sinuses, elevated orifices, volcano-like sinuses
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma displays crateriform sinus openings with raised, elevated, papular margins reminiscent of miniature volcanoes on the skin surface.

relationships.keywords: interconnected fistulae, branching sinuses, fascial tunnels
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma exhibits interconnected fistulous tracts where pressure applied over one nodule expresses purulent grain-laden exudate from adjacent distant orifices.

relationships.keywords: serosanguinous drainage, blood-tinged fluid, sinus exudate
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma displays continuous serosanguinous sinus drainage, intermittently staining dressings with oily, blood-tinged fluid containing grains.

relationships.keywords: oily discharge, purulent fluid, viscous exudate
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma produces an oily purulent discharge containing sebum-like lipids and degenerated granulomatous debris along with microcolonies.

relationships.keywords: absence of pain, non-tender mass, anesthetic lesion
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Mycetoma displays a striking absence of pain in over 85% of patients despite massive anatomical deformity and bone invasion, likely due to localized anesthetic metabolites.

relationships.keywords: afebrile state, normal temperature, absence of fever
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma presents with an afebrile clinical presentation, maintaining normal systemic body temperature in the absence of secondary pyogenic superinfection.

relationships.keywords: absence of erythema, cold mass, lack of redness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma typically demonstrates an absence of active erythema surrounding early nodules, appearing as a cold mass unlike acute pyogenic abscesses.

relationships.keywords: skin hyperpigmentation, melanoderma, dark skin overlying
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma exhibits local skin hyperpigmentation and brawny skin thickening directly overlying long-standing deep granulomatous deposits.

relationships.keywords: cutaneous tethering, skin dimpling, deep anchoring
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma demonstrates cutaneous tethering to the underlying mass, preventing the skin from being pinched or mobilized independently.

relationships.keywords: fascial fixation, immobility on contraction, anchored mass
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma exhibits deep fascial fixation where the tumefactive mass becomes completely immobile when underlying muscles are actively contracted.

relationships.keywords: puckered scars, healed sinuses, retracted cicatrices
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma displays puckered scar orifices where older sinus tracts have temporarily healed, leaving retracted, pitted cicatricial depressions.

relationships.keywords: lobulated mass, nodular contours, multinodular swelling
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma displays lobulated subcutaneous contours upon palpation, reflecting multiple aggregated granulomatous chambers separated by fibrous septa.

relationships.keywords: preserved sensation, intact nerves, sensory preservation
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma typically shows preserved distal peripheral sensation, differentiating it from neurotrophic neuropathies and lepromatous anesthesia.

relationships.keywords: intact pulses, dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial artery
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma maintains preserved peripheral arterial pulses (dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial) because major vascular conduits are displaced rather than occluded.

relationships.keywords: painless lymphadenopathy, regional nodes, mobile nodes
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma presents with painless regional lymphadenopathy where draining lymph nodes are firm, rubbery, and non-tender on physical palpation.

relationships.keywords: sentinel nodules, satellite nodules, subcutaneous beads
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma displays firm mobile sentinel nodules along the lymphatic channels proximal to the primary mass, indicating regional lymphatic dissemination.

relationships.keywords: normal temperature, absence of calor, cold tumefaction
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma demonstrates normal local skin temperature on manual examination, lacking the calor and thermal elevation seen in acute pyogenic infections.

relationships.keywords: false healing, cyclical reopening, chronic recurrence
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Mycetoma demonstrates false healing with scarring where sinuses temporarily close only to erupt into fresh discharging orifices weeks later.

relationships.keywords: dot in circle, MRI sign, pathognomonic MRI, T2 weighted
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma displays the pathognomonic MRI dot-in-circle sign on T2-weighted and STIR sequences, showing high-signal granulomatous spheres surrounding low-signal central grain dots.

relationships.keywords: T2 hyperintensity, granuloma spheres, MRI bright signal
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma demonstrates T2-weighted hyperintense round granulomas reflecting fluid-filled inflammatory tissue and interstitial edema surrounding grains.

relationships.keywords: hypointense dot, central grain, magnetic susceptibility
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma exhibits a central hypointense grain dot on MRI due to magnetic susceptibility effects and fibrous/cement matrix within the microbial grain.

relationships.keywords: gadolinium enhancement, rim enhancement, contrast MRI
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma shows peripheral gadolinium rim enhancement on contrast-enhanced MRI, demarcating fibrous encapsulating collagen rings around granulomas.

relationships.keywords: ultrasound sign, dot in circle US, POCUS hallmark
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma demonstrates the ultrasound dot-in-circle sign on point-of-care high-resolution sonography, revealing round hypoechoic granulomas containing bright central echoes.

relationships.keywords: hyper-reflective echoes, bright echoes, sonographic grains
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma displays central hyper-reflective echoes on bedside POCUS representing the dense microbial microcolonies within fluid-filled cavities.

relationships.keywords: acoustic shadowing, sonographic shadow, cement attenuation
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma demonstrates posterior acoustic shadowing beneath central grain echoes on ultrasound, particularly prominent with hard melanized Madurella grains.

relationships.keywords: thick-walled cavities, hypoechoic lesions, eumycetoma US
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma exhibits thick-walled hypoechoic granulomas on sonography, highly characteristic of fungal eumycetoma reflecting fibrous pseudo-capsules.

relationships.keywords: ill-defined US, actinomycetoma sonography, diffuse infiltrates
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma exhibits ill-defined hypoechoic infiltrates on ultrasound in bacterial actinomycetoma, lacking distinct capsules and showing diffuse infiltrative margins.

relationships.keywords: moth eaten bone, bone destruction, plain X-ray
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma displays a characteristic moth-eaten bone appearance on plain radiographs, showing multiple small irregular osteolytic cavities across tarsal and metatarsal bones.

relationships.keywords: geodes, punched out cavities, bone cysts, X-ray
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma exhibits multiple punched-out osteolytic geodes with sclerotic margins on plain X-rays, representing intraosseous granulomatous expansion.

relationships.keywords: periosteal reaction, hyperostosis, sunburst/spiculation
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma demonstrates prominent periosteal cortical bone reaction with new bone deposition and cortical thickening surrounding osteolytic pockets.

relationships.keywords: preserved joint spaces, articular preservation, cartilage sparing
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma displays preserved articular joint spaces on plain radiographs despite massive neighboring bone destruction, distinguishing it from pyogenic septic arthritis.

relationships.keywords: soft tissue swelling, plane loss, fascial blunting
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma shows extensive soft tissue plane obliteration on plain radiography, with diffuse density replacing normal fat fascial interfaces.

relationships.keywords: cortical remodeling, bone expansion, melting sugar
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma causes cortical bone remodeling and bony expansion with a 'melting sugar' radiographic appearance due to simultaneous osteolysis and sclerosis.

relationships.keywords: CT bone erosion, cortical breach, CT osteolysis
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma displays CT cortical bone erosion with precise delineation of minute cortical breaches and intraosseous grain-containing cavities.

relationships.keywords: CT soft tissue, muscle invasion, preoperative mapping
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Mycetoma demonstrates CT soft-tissue infiltration mapping the full 3D extent of granulomatous tracts through muscular and subcutaneous layers.

relationships.keywords: direct wet mount, grain cytology, bedside microscopy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma triage relies on direct grain wet mount of extruded discharge, providing immediate microscopic differentiation between fungal and bacterial grains.

relationships.keywords: KOH mount, 10% KOH, fungal digestion, grain cytology
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits characteristic broad hyphae on 10-20% potassium hydroxide grain mount, which digests host debris and unmasks fungal filaments.

relationships.keywords: broad hyphae, septate hyphae, 2-6 um, eumycetoma microscopy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma direct cytology reveals broad septate fungal hyphae (2 to 6 micrometers wide) diagnostic of fungal eumycetoma.

relationships.keywords: chlamydoconidia, vesicular cells, swollen hyphae, Madurella
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma grain cytology demonstrates vesicular swollen chlamydoconidia (up to 15-25 micrometers) embedded at the periphery of fungal grains.

relationships.keywords: cement matrix, melanized cement, brown pigment, Madurella
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma microscopy reveals an amorphous brown-black cement matrix composed of oxidized melanin and heavy metals embedding fungal hyphae.

relationships.keywords: Gram-positive filaments, thin filaments, <1 um, actinomycete
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma grain smears demonstrate delicate Gram-positive filaments (<1 micrometer wide) with branching, diagnostic of bacterial actinomycetoma.

relationships.keywords: bacterial microcolonies, actinomycete clumps, grain smear
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma cytology displays branching bacterial microcolonies forming compact aggregates with peripheral ray-like projections.

relationships.keywords: modified Kinyoun, acid fast, Nocardia staining
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits modified Kinyoun stain positivity with 1% sulfuric acid decolorization, specifically identifying Nocardia species.

relationships.keywords: partially acid-fast, Nocardia filaments, red branching filaments
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma reveals partially acid-fast filaments on modified acid-fast stains, distinguishing Nocardia from non-acid-fast Actinomadura and Streptomyces.

relationships.keywords: suppurative granuloma, neutrophils, histiocytes, pathology
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma histopathology demonstrates a classic suppurative granulomatous reaction, with central neutrophilic microabscesses surrounding grains enclosed by histiocytes and giant cells.

relationships.keywords: Splendore Hoeppli, asteroid bodies, eosinophilic precipitate
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma histopathology frequently demonstrates the Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon, showing radiating eosinophilic proteinaceous deposits around grains.

relationships.keywords: PAS stain, periodic acid Schiff, fungal cell wall
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma histopathology shows strongly PAS-positive fungal elements with magenta cell walls highlighting fungal hyphal morphology.

relationships.keywords: Grocott silver, GMS stain, black fungal wall
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma sections exhibit Grocott methenamine silver positivity, staining fungal cell walls sharply black against a light green counterstain.

relationships.keywords: elevated ESR, 40-80 mm/h, chronic inflammation, erythrocyte sedimentation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits moderate-to-severe erythrocyte sedimentation rate elevation (40 to 80 mm/h) reflecting chronic localized granulomatous turnover.

relationships.keywords: normal WBC, absence of leukocytosis, normal CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma admission testing demonstrates a normal peripheral leukocyte count, lacking systemic leukocytosis in uncomplicated cases.

relationships.keywords: no eosinophilia, normal eosinophils, non-parasitic profile
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits an absence of peripheral eosinophilia on differential leukocyte count, differentiating it from invasive helminthic granulomas.

relationships.keywords: normal neutrophils, no left shift, lack of neutrophilia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits an absence of neutrophilia and absent toxic left shift on peripheral blood smear, distinguishing it from acute pyogenic cellulitis.

relationships.keywords: normocytic anemia, anemia of chronic disease, hemoglobin low
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma frequently exhibits mild normocytic normochromic anemia of chronic disease in patients with multi-year disease burdens.

relationships.keywords: FNA, fine needle aspiration, grain cytology, intact nodule
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma is rapidly diagnosed via fine-needle aspiration grain cytology from intact subcutaneous nodules before sinuses ulcerate.

relationships.keywords: deep biopsy, surgical biopsy, histopathology gold standard
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma evaluation utilizes deep surgical biopsy histopathology to obtain intact tissue grains and determine bone and fascial margin involvement.

relationships.keywords: Sabouraud agar, fungal culture, slow growth, Madurella culture
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mycetoma exhibits slow fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar without cycloheximide, growing brown-to-black colonies after 2 to 6 weeks at 30°C.

relationships.keywords: mycetoma belt, geographic distribution, 15N to 30N, tropics
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma has high endemic transmission in the Mycetoma Belt, spanning arid tropical and subtropical territories between latitudes 15°S and 30°N.

relationships.keywords: arid climate, low rainfall, 50-500 mm rain, desert scrub
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma is strongly associated with exposure to arid and semi-arid climates characterized by low annual rainfall (50-500 mm) and high ambient temperatures.

relationships.keywords: Acacia thorns, acacia nilotica, plant thorns, percutaneous trauma
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma transmission commonly occurs through traumatic puncture from Acacia nilotica thorns that carry soil-dwelling fungi and actinomycetes into subcutaneous tissue.

relationships.keywords: penetrating trauma, skin puncture, microtrauma, inoculation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma requires minor penetrating skin trauma to breach the stratum corneum and introduce environmental saprophytes into the subcutaneous compartment.

relationships.keywords: barefoot walking, lack of shoes, unprotected feet, pedal trauma
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma is linked to barefoot walking in rural fields and scrubland, predisposing individuals to frequent penetrating pedal injuries.

relationships.keywords: soil microorganisms, saprophytic fungi, geophilic actinomycetes
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma infection occurs via direct contact with soil-dwelling microorganisms that survive saprophytically in arid topsoil and decayed thorny vegetation.

relationships.keywords: plant splinters, wood splinters, vegetable matter puncture
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma inoculation frequently occurs through puncture from dry plant splinters and dried shrub debris during agricultural foraging.

relationships.keywords: wood chips, timber handling, carpenter trauma, puncture
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma transmission is linked to skin puncture from wood chips and splintered firewood handled by manual workers.

relationships.keywords: carrying firewood, back trauma, shoulder lesions, wood bundles
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma of the upper back and shoulder is acquired through carrying thorny firewood bundles directly on bare shoulders and upper trunk.

relationships.keywords: crop sacks, soil sacks, agricultural bags, shoulder trauma
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma of the dorsal trunk occurs in field hands through carrying soil-laden crop sacks contaminated with thorny plant residue.

relationships.keywords: Sudan, Gezira state, hyperendemic region, Khartoum
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma has its highest recorded global disease burden in Sudan Gezira state, representing the world's most hyperendemic focus for Madurella mycetomatis.

relationships.keywords: Mexico, Morelos, San Luis Potosi, actinomycetoma capital
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma is hyperendemic across central and northern Mexico, recognized as the global epicenter of actinomycetoma predominantly caused by Nocardia brasiliensis.

relationships.keywords: Rajasthan, northwest India, Thar desert, Indian mycetoma
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma is highly prevalent across arid northwest India (particularly Rajasthan), where both fungal and bacterial agents cause heavy community disease burdens.

relationships.keywords: farmers, agriculturalists, rural field workers, cultivators
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Mycetoma predominantly infects rural subsistence farmers who engage in manual soil cultivation and crop harvesting without protective boots.

relationships.keywords: farm laborers, field hands, day laborers, agricultural work
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Mycetoma disproportionately affects field agricultural laborers subject to recurrent penetrating plant trauma and prolonged outdoor soil contact.

relationships.keywords: pastoralists, herdsmen, livestock keepers, nomadic shepherds
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Mycetoma frequently afflicts nomadic livestock pastoralists and herdsmen walking vast distances barefoot through thorny acacia terrain.

relationships.keywords: young men, 15 to 40 years, male preponderance, 3:1 ratio
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Mycetoma displays a marked demographic skew toward young adult males aged 15 to 40 years, with a male-to-female ratio between 3:1 and 4:1.

relationships.keywords: poverty, low socioeconomic status, rural villages, neglected disease
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Mycetoma is concentrated among impoverished rural communities lacking footwear, sanitation, health awareness, and access to secondary medical care.

relationships.keywords: indolent incubation, multi-year progression, insidious onset
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Mycetoma exhibits an indolent multi-year incubation period, slowly developing from a tiny microscopic focus into a palpable nodule over months to decades.

relationships.keywords: two to five years, clinical latency, consultation delay
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Mycetoma patients present with an average two-to-five-year onset period between initial percutaneous thorn injury and their first medical evaluation.

relationships.keywords: dormancy, slow organization, cement formation, grain latency
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Mycetoma involves prolonged subcutaneous fungal dormancy, as spores slowly aggregate and synthesize protective cement before clinical eruption.

relationships.keywords: non-contagious, no person to person, environmental only
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Mycetoma displays strictly non-contagious transmission, requiring environmental percutaneous inoculation with zero recorded instances of person-to-person spread.

relationships.keywords: acute onset, rapid course, days to weeks, cellulitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by acute rapid progression evolving over days to weeks, which indicates acute bacterial cellulitis or necrotizing fasciitis.

relationships.keywords: severe pain, throbbing pain, acute tenderness, pyogenic
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by acute severe localized pain at disease onset, which is characteristic of pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis or acute abscesses.

relationships.keywords: high fever, rigor, chills, pyrexia, septic syndrome
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by high spiking fevers, chills, and rigors at initial presentation, which point toward acute pyogenic sepsis or disseminated bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: neutrophilic leukocytosis, left shift, toxic granulation, high WBC
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by marked neutrophilic leukocytosis with significant left shift and bandemia, typical of acute bacterial pyogenic infections.

relationships.keywords: no grains, absence of granules, negative exudate, sterile sinus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Typical active mycetoma is ruled out by the complete absence of grains upon microscopic and visual examination of multiple discharging sinuses.

relationships.keywords: visceral metastasis, hematogenous spread, lung lesions, spleen
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by rapid hematogenous dissemination to internal viscera (lungs, brain, spleen), as mycetoma spreads strictly by contiguous tissue invasion.

relationships.keywords: medlar bodies, copper pennies, muriform cells, chromoblastomycosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by the presence of pigmented medlar bodies copper pennies (muriform cells) on microscopic examination, which establishes chromoblastomycosis.

relationships.keywords: fluctuant abscess, acute collection, hot abscess, pus pocket
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by an acute fluctuant pyogenic abscess with erythema and warmth, which represents staphylococcal or streptococcal soft-tissue infection.

relationships.keywords: necrotizing ulcer, gangrene, rapid tissue necrosis, ulceration
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by rapid necrotizing ulceration destroying superficial skin within days, pointing toward necrotizing fasciitis or pyoderma gangrenosum.

relationships.keywords: contagious spread, household transmission, person to person
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by documented human-to-human transmission between family members, as it is strictly acquired through environmental percutaneous inoculation.

relationships.keywords: bilateral lymphedema, podoconiosis, elephantiasis, mossy foot
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Primary mycetoma is ruled out by symmetrical bilateral ascending lymphedema without localized tumefaction or sinuses, which defines podoconiosis or filariasis.

relationships.keywords: caseating granulomas, Ziehl-Neelsen, AFB positive, tuberculosis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by caseating granulomas with AFB on standard Ziehl-Neelsen staining, which establishes Mycobacterium tuberculosis osteoarticular infection.

relationships.keywords: malignant spindle cells, osteosarcoma histology, sarcoma cells
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by malignant anaplastic spindle cells and osteoid matrix on histological biopsy, confirming osteosarcoma or soft tissue sarcoma.

relationships.keywords: spontaneous cure, self-limiting, natural resolution
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by spontaneous clinical resolution without prolonged antimicrobial therapy, as untreated mycetoma is inexorably chronic and progressive.

relationships.keywords: espundia, midface destruction, mucosal leishmaniasis, palate ulcer
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by destructive mucocutaneous midface ulceration of the nasal septum and palate, which defines mucocutaneous leishmaniasis.

relationships.keywords: superficial plaques, verrucous skin, warty lesion, no deep mass
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by purely superficial verrucous plaques confined to the epidermis without deep subcutaneous tumefaction or bone changes.

relationships.keywords: painful lymphadenitis, tender bubo, acute adenitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated mycetoma is ruled out by acute, exquisitely painful regional lymphadenitis with suppurative bubo formation at presentation.

relationships.keywords: toxic shock, septic shock, hypotension, organ failure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by acute diffuse systemic toxic shock with hypotension and multiorgan failure at initial presentation.

relationships.keywords: penicillin cure, short-course penicillin, rapid antibiotic cure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by rapid complete clinical cure within 10 to 14 days of standard penicillin therapy, which indicates actinomycosis or streptococcal disease.

relationships.keywords: microfilariae, Wuchereria bancrofti, nocturnal smear, filariasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by demonstration of Wuchereria bancrofti microfilaremia on nocturnal thick blood smears, which confirms lymphatic filariasis.

relationships.keywords: bone sequestrum, chronic osteomyelitis, Brodie abscess, no sinuses
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by isolated intraosseous bone sequestration without external draining cutaneous sinuses or grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: pulmonary metastasis, lung nodules, cannonball lesions, malignancy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Mycetoma is ruled out by spontaneous pulmonary metastatic nodules on chest radiography, confirming metastatic mesenchymal malignancy.

relationships.keywords: osteomyelitis, Staphylococcus aureus, bone pain, fever, pyogenic sinuses
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from chronic pyogenic osteomyelitis, which causes severe localized bone pain, recurring fevers, acute neutrophilic leukocytosis, and purulent discharge lacking macroscopic pigmented grains.

relationships.keywords: chromoblastomycosis, Fonsecaea, verrucous plaques, medlar bodies, copper pennies
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from chromoblastomycosis, which forms superficial warty cauliflower-like verrucous plaques with black surface dots and diagnostic medlar bodies, lacking deep bone invasion, geodes, or grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: osteosarcoma, bone malignancy, sunburst periosteum, Codman triangle, no sinuses
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from osteosarcoma, which manifests with rapid aggressive bone destruction, severe night pain, sunburst periosteal reaction, and Codman triangles without draining cutaneous sinus tracts or grains.

relationships.keywords: Kaposi sarcoma, HHV-8, violaceous plaques, spindle cells, vascular neoplasm
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Kaposi Sarcoma, which presents as violaceous vascular cutaneous plaques and nodules with spindle-cell proliferation and HHV-8 positivity, lacking deep osteolytic geodes, sinus tracts, and grains.

relationships.keywords: tuberculosis, cutaneous TB, lupus vulgaris, tuberculous osteomyelitis, AFB
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Tuberculosis (tuberculous osteomyelitis and lupus vulgaris), which exhibits caseating necrosis, positive acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain, and tuberculin reactivity without discharging pigmented grains.

relationships.keywords: podoconiosis, non-filarial elephantiasis, volcanic soil, bilateral lymphedema
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from podoconiosis, which causes bilateral ascending non-pitting lymphedema, hyperkeratosis, and mossy foot lesions in volcanic soil regions without discharging sinus tracts or bone geodes.

relationships.keywords: filariasis, elephantiasis, Wuchereria bancrofti, microfilariae, lymphangitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Lymphatic Filariasis, which causes diffuse lower extremity and genital elephantiasis with retrograde adenolymphangitis and nocturnal microfilaremia without localized sinus tracts or grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: leishmaniasis, Leishmania tropica, oriental sore, LD bodies, ulcer
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Cutaneous Leishmaniasis, which presents with painless crusted skin ulcers with raised indurated borders containing intracellular Leishmania amastigotes, without deep fascial tracking or grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: leprosy, Mycobacterium leprae, nerve thickening, anesthesia, hypopigmented macules
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Leprosy, which features peripheral nerve thickening, glove-and-stocking sensory anesthesia, hypopigmented skin macules, and acid-fast Mycobacterium leprae, without discharging grain sinuses.

relationships.keywords: soft tissue sarcoma, liposarcoma, fibrosarcoma, deep painless mass, malignancy
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from soft tissue sarcoma, which presents as a rapidly enlarging painless deep fascial mass without cutaneous fistulae, sinus openings, or microbial grain discharge.

relationships.keywords: actinomycosis, Actinomyces israelii, sulfur granules, cervicofacial, penicillin
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from actinomycosis, which arises from endogenous mucosal flora (Actinomyces israelii) following mucosal injury, predominantly involves cervicofacial or thoracoabdominal sites, and responds promptly to high-dose penicillin.

relationships.keywords: sporotrichosis, Sporothrix schenckii, rose gardener, sporotrichoid, asteroid bodies
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from sporotrichosis, which manifests as nodular lymphangitic tracking (sporotrichoid spread) proximal to the inoculation site with cigar-shaped budding yeasts, lacking extensive bone geodes and grains.

relationships.keywords: cellulitis, erysipelas, streptococcus, acute redness, warmth, fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from bacterial cellulitis, which presents acutely with spreading erythema, localized calor, severe tenderness, high fever, and prompt response to beta-lactam antibiotics without sinus tracts or grains.

relationships.keywords: Buruli ulcer, Mycobacterium ulcerans, mycolactone, necrotic ulcer, painless
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from Buruli ulcer, which causes extensive painless subcutaneous necrosis and large undermined cutaneous ulcers mediated by mycolactone toxin, without grain-discharging sinuses or moth-eaten bone geodes.

relationships.keywords: melioidosis, Burkholderia pseudomallei, septicemia, visceral abscesses, soil
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from melioidosis, which presents as acute septicemia or multiple visceral microabscesses (spleen, liver, prostate) caused by safety-pin Gram-negative Burkholderia pseudomallei without grain-laden sinuses.

relationships.keywords: chondrosarcoma, cartilage tumor, ring and arc calcification, no sinuses
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from chondrosarcoma, which shows chondroid matrix 'rings and arcs' calcifications on imaging and malignant cartilaginous histology without discharging cutaneous sinuses or microbial grains.

relationships.keywords: foreign body granuloma, thorn granuloma, retained wood, localized nodule
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma is differentiated from foreign body granuloma, which produces a small localized non-progressive sterile nodule around retained plant material without multiple interconnected sinuses, grain shedding, or progressive bone destruction.

relationships.keywords: eumycetoma vs actinomycetoma, fungal vs bacterial, medical cure, Welsh regimen
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Mycetoma subtypes are differentiated internally: eumycetoma produces black/white grains with thick fungal hyphae and requires prolonged azoles plus surgery, whereas actinomycetoma yields red/yellow grains with delicate bacterial filaments and achieves >90% medical cure with the Welsh regimen without surgery.
